newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokai Kogyo decides to apply for court protection.
newsitem.headline: Tokai Kogyo decides to apply for court protection.

text.p: Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd said on Friday that its board members have decided that the construction firm will apply for court protection under Japanese bankruptcy laws.
When a company applies for court protection from creditors under Japanese law, the move is widely regarded as a sign that the company is on the verge of failing.
Jiji new agency, quoting unnamed sources, reported that the company had debts totalling 520 billion yen.
A Tokai Kogyo spokesman said: "The board has resolved to apply for court protection."
He declined to reveal the amount of the company's debts or say why it decided to make the court application.
Media reports said the company fell into difficulties as it was unable to sell its real estate assets due a sharp fall in land prices and faced declining profits in its condominium business.
The reports also said banks had refused to cut the interest rates on their loans to Tokai Kogyo.
A spokesman for Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, which is a major lender to the company, said the bank would lead other lenders in hammering out measures to help Tokai Kogyo rebuild its business.
A spokesman for Norinchukin Bank, a farmers' bank, said it expected to give up part of the loans it had extended to the company.
"Lenders will have to consider providing funds to the company so it can continue its operations," the spokesman said.
A spokesman for Tokai Kokyo said the company expects to hold a news conference at 6 p.m. (0900 GMT) on Friday at the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
